help.how_to_guides_subtitle: Each guide walks you through one task on the real pages. You do the clicks; the guide shows the way.

ui.your_turn: Your turn: the guide moves on when you have done this.

console_tour.title: Tour of the console
console_tour.description: A minute's look at where things are.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.body: Your starting point: what needs attention, what is running and how much it is used. The Getting started list stays here until you hide it.

infrastructure.title: AI Infrastructure
infrastructure.body: Your own hardware and the models on it. Machines are the computers with GPUs, a cluster groups machines that serve models together, the Model marketplace is where you pick a model to host, and Deployments shows what runs where.

llm.title: LLM
llm.body: Providers connects models that run elsewhere, such as OpenAI or Azure, next to your own. The API endpoint is the one OpenAI-compatible address that applications use for all of them.

chat.title: Chat
chat.body: Opens the chat, where people talk to the models you host or connect. Everyone with an account can use it.

agents.title: Agents
agents.body: Agents work inside other software, such as Word, Outlook or the browser, with the models and rules you set here. Governance decides which tools chats and agents may use.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Finds personal data, such as names, email addresses or account numbers, in what people send, and masks it before it reaches a model. The policies decide what is found and what happens to it.

access.title: Access Control
access.body: Who may do what: users, roles with their permissions, and groups. Roles count in the chat and through the API; the console is for superusers. With the sign-in module, people sign in with their company account.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.body: MCP servers give chats and agents tools, such as search, tickets or files. Skills are instructions people save once and reuse in the chat.

help.title: Help
help.body: Open this menu any time. About this page (or F1) explains the page you are on, Getting started brings back the setup list, and the how-to guides walk you through tasks on the real pages.

add_machine.title: Add a machine
add_machine.description: Connect a computer with a GPU so it can run models.

open.title: Add a machine
open.body: Click Add a machine. Any Linux computer with an NVIDIA GPU that can reach this server will do.

command.title: Run this on the machine
command.body: Copy the command and run it in a terminal on the machine you are adding. It installs a small agent, shows a short code and waits for you.

approve.title: Approve it here
approve.body: The machine shows up here a moment later. Check that its code matches the one in its terminal, then click Approve.

unattended.title: Adding many machines?
unattended.body: Skip the approval step puts a single-use token into the command, so a machine joins on its own: for scripts, Ansible or images. Close this panel when you are done.

create_cluster.title: Create a cluster
create_cluster.description: Group your machines so they can serve models together.

open.title: Create a cluster
open.body: Click Create a cluster. It needs at least one machine.

name.title: Name it
name.body: Give the cluster a short name, such as gpu-room, then click Next.

machines.title: Pick the machines
machines.body: Tick the machines that should serve models; one machine makes a fine cluster, and you can add more later from the cluster's page. Then click Next; the console checks how the machines reach each other.

network.title: The network
network.body: The console suggests the fastest network the machines share. Keep the suggestion unless you know better.

start.title: Create it
start.body: Click Create cluster. The machines start it in the background, and the cluster's page shows how far it got. Next step: host a model on it.

host_model.title: Host a model
host_model.description: Pick a model from the marketplace and run it on your cluster.

fit.title: Fit for cluster
fit.body: Every model is checked against this cluster's GPUs and memory. With several clusters, pick the one you want to host on.

tabs.title: Find a model
tabs.body: Recommended lists models known to work well, Search Hugging Face finds any other, and On this server shows the ones already downloaded.

card.title: A model
card.body: Each card says what the model is for and whether it fits. Click the card for the details.

host.title: Host it
host.body: Click Host on the model you want.

where.title: Where it runs
where.body: Pick the cluster, how many GPUs each copy uses and how many copies run. You see right away whether it fits. Then click Next.

settings.title: Engine settings
settings.body: The suggested settings suit most uses. Change the context length here if people need longer conversations. Then click Next.

review.title: Review and host
review.body: Check the two names: the deployment's, and the one people pick in the chat. Then click Host. The server downloads the model, copies it to the machines and starts it; Deployments shows how far it got.

connect_provider.title: Connect a cloud model
connect_provider.description: Use models from OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic or another provider next to your own.

name.title: Name it
name.body: A name people will recognize, such as OpenAI.

target.title: Where the model runs
target.body: Choose Remote Endpoint for a provider on the internet.

kind.title: The provider
kind.body: Pick the provider. Its address is filled in for you. For any other OpenAI-compatible service, choose OpenAI-compatible and enter its address.

key.title: API key and model
key.body: Paste the API key from the provider's console, then pick the model. The key stays on this server; people using the chat never see it.

test.title: Test it
test.body: Test Connection sends a tiny request to check the key and the address. Then click Next.

pricing.title: Prices
pricing.body: Optional: the provider's prices per million tokens, so the console can show what usage costs. You can leave them empty.

create.title: Create it
create.body: Click Create. The model is then available in the chat and through the API.

invite_people.title: Add people
invite_people.description: Create accounts so your colleagues can use the chat.

account.title: Their sign-in
account.body: Their email address and a first password of at least 6 characters. Pass the password on to them in person or by phone.

roles.title: What they may do
roles.body: Leave the roles empty for people who only chat: they get the standard user role. Roles you tick replace it, so for someone who should also chat, tick default_user as well. Roles decide what people may do in the chat and through the API; the console itself is for superusers. Then click Create User.

create_api_token.title: Create an API token
create_api_token.description: A token lets scripts and applications use the models through the API.

name.title: Name
name.body: Name the token after what will use it, such as build server, so you know which one to revoke later.

lifetime.title: Lifetime
lifetime.body: How long the token works. Shorter is safer; you can always create a new one.

value.title: Copy it now
value.body: The token is shown only this once. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe.

list.title: Your tokens
list.body: All your tokens are listed here. Revoke one as soon as it is no longer needed or may have leaked.

checklist.title: Getting started
checklist.subtitle: From a fresh install to people using it. Each step ticks itself when it is done.
checklist.done_body: Machines, a cluster, a model and people: everything is in place. You can hide this list; it stays under Help.

machine.title: Add a machine
machine.body: Connect a computer with a GPU.

cluster.title: Create a cluster
cluster.body: Group your machines so they can serve models.

model.title: Host a model
model.body: Pick a model from the marketplace and start it on your cluster.

chat.title: Try it in the chat
chat.body: Talk to your model the way your colleagues will.

provider.title: Connect a cloud model
provider.body: Use OpenAI, Azure and others next to your own models.

privacy.title: Set a privacy policy
privacy.body: Decide which personal data is masked before it reaches a model.

tools.title: Connect tools
tools.body: Add an MCP server so chats and agents can search, open tickets and more.

skills.title: Add a skill
skills.body: Save instructions people reuse in the chat.

agents.title: Set up an agent
agents.body: Let Office, the browser or your own applications use the models, under your rules.

token.title: Create an API token
token.body: For scripts and applications that call the API.

tour.title: Take the console tour
tour.body: A minute's look at where things are.

unknown.title: About this page
unknown.description: There is no help for this page yet. The Help menu has the Getting started list and the how-to guides.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Your platform at a glance: what needs attention, traffic, capacity and health. Each card loads on its own.
dashboard.action_getting_started: Follow the Getting started list until everything is set up
dashboard.action_attention: See what needs attention, and mute what you already know about
dashboard.action_customize: Customize: drag, resize, show or hide cards; your layout follows you to other devices
dashboard.action_status: The status pill at the top sums up the platform's health

containers.title: Containers
containers.description: Everything Docker runs on this server. What you may do with a container depends on its class: system containers need Root Mode to stop or delete, untrusted ones cannot be stopped at all.
containers.action_filter: Click a tile or pick a class to filter the list
containers.action_control: Start, stop, pause, restart or delete a container from its row
containers.action_class: Change a container's class (SYSTEM_CORE stays locked)
containers.action_create: Create a container from an image already on this server

create_container.title: Create container
create_container.description: Run a new container from an image that is already on this server. Pull the image under Images first.
create_container.action_image: Pick the image, a name and, if needed, a command
create_container.action_config: Add ports, environment variables and volumes
create_container.action_class: Set the class, policy and network; start it right away or later

edit_container.title: Edit container
edit_container.description: Editing replaces the container: a new one starts with the new settings, and files outside its volumes are lost.
edit_container.action_change: Change the image, ports, variables or volumes
edit_container.action_save: Save and replace when you are ready

container_detail.title: Container
container_detail.description: One container: its state, image, networks and logs.
container_detail.action_logs: Read the last 300 log lines, refresh or download them
container_detail.action_exec: Start an exec session for a websocket client; outside tenant apps this needs Root Mode

images.title: Images
images.description: The Docker images on this server.
images.action_pull: Pull an image, with live progress
images.action_prune: Prune dangling images; try a dry run first (needs Root Mode)

networks.title: Networks
networks.description: The Docker networks on this server. System networks are read-only.
networks.action_create: Create a network, optionally internal (no outbound access)
networks.action_inspect: Inspect a network and the containers on it

stacks.title: Stacks
stacks.description: Docker Compose stacks deployed from here, with every revision kept.
stacks.action_deploy: Deploy a stack from a compose file; the same ID makes a new revision
stacks.action_rollback: Roll back to an earlier revision

observability.title: Cost Observability
observability.description: Cost, usage and speed of the requests the gateway served. Costs are estimates from the prices you set; they do not affect billing.
observability.action_overview: Spend, requests, tokens, latency and errors over 7 to 90 days
observability.action_requests: Browse requests, filter by model or user, and open one to see its pipeline
observability.action_pricing: Set the prices per million tokens

logs.title: Logs & Audit
logs.description: Logs from every machine and container, and the audit trail of who changed what.
logs.action_filter: Filter by machine or source, time and text; follow new lines live
logs.action_audit: Switch to Audit for actions, targets, results and who did them

security_map.title: Data Residency
security_map.description: Where your prompts are processed: on your machines, in your network, or outside it.
security_map.action_residency: See which providers are local, external or unknown
security_map.action_where: Say where a provider sends prompts when it cannot be detected
security_map.action_volume: See how much data goes where

agent_trace.title: LLM Calls
agent_trace.description: How providers, runtimes and models connect, and the calls going through them as they happen.
agent_trace.action_graph: Search and filter the graph; click a node for its details
agent_trace.action_live: Watch calls arrive; pause and resume the stream

endpoint.title: API Endpoint
endpoint.description: The documentation of the gateway's OpenAI-compatible API: the one address applications use for every model.
endpoint.action_docs: Browse the API documentation, or open it in a new tab
endpoint.action_container: Start, stop or restart the gateway container

runtime_detail.title: Runtime
runtime_detail.description: A single-container model runtime, the one behind a Local Docker provider.
runtime_detail.action_config: Edit its configuration, then save and restart

providers.title: LLM Providers
providers.description: Every model the gateway can reach: on your clusters, in a local container, or at a cloud provider. Models deployed on a cluster appear here by themselves.
providers.action_add: Add a provider: a cloud API with its key, or a local container
providers.action_test: Test the connection; it also lists the provider's models
providers.action_price: Set a price, so costs show up under Cost Observability
providers.action_manage: Edit, start, stop or delete a provider; cluster deployments are managed on their own page

node_profiles.title: Machine Profiles
node_profiles.description: Reusable settings for machines: runtime, GPU, storage, network, logging, security and updates.
node_profiles.action_create: Create a profile from JSON settings
node_profiles.action_assign: Assign a profile to a machine on that machine's page

node_detail.title: Machine
node_detail.description: One machine: its hardware, logs, deployments, the vLLM it runs, its commands and updates.
node_detail.action_status: See its hardware, deployments and recent logs
node_detail.action_maintenance: Drain it (its copies move to the other machines first), or put it in maintenance
node_detail.action_updates: Check for and install system updates, or reboot it
node_detail.action_vllm: Route a vLLM found on it through Fadenstack

nodes.title: Machines
nodes.description: The computers with GPUs that run your models. A machine joins by running one command on it and being approved here.
nodes.action_add: Add a machine: run the command on it, then approve it here
nodes.action_status: See each machine's status, GPUs and agent version
nodes.action_maintenance: Drain a machine to move its model copies to the other machines; maintenance marks it for servicing
nodes.action_delete: Delete a machine (type its name to confirm)

cluster_detail.title: Cluster
cluster_detail.description: One cluster: its machines, how they are wired, the models on it and their traffic.
cluster_detail.action_wiring: See how its machines are wired, and change the network
cluster_detail.action_security: Encrypt model traffic and the traffic between machines
cluster_detail.action_runtime: Switch the runtime version (this restarts the models)
cluster_detail.action_control: Stop, start or delete it; delete its deployments first
cluster_detail.action_machines: Add machines, or remove one (its copies move to the others first)

clusters.title: Clusters
clusters.description: A cluster groups machines so they can serve models together. You can create one once a machine is connected.
clusters.action_create: Create a cluster: name it, pick its machines, confirm the network
clusters.action_open: Open a cluster to see its machines and models
clusters.action_found: Take over a cluster your machines still run but this server lost

marketplace.title: Model marketplace
marketplace.description: Find a model, see whether it fits your clusters, and host it.
marketplace.action_find: Browse recommended models, or search Hugging Face
marketplace.action_fit: Pick a cluster to see which models fit on it
marketplace.action_host: Host a model: where it runs, engine settings, review
marketplace.action_local: See and manage the models already on this server
marketplace.action_token: Gated models need a Hugging Face token (the button at the top)

deployment_detail.title: Deployment
deployment_detail.description: One model running on a cluster: its health, copies, machines, speed and logs.
deployment_detail.action_scale: Scale it: more copies, or a different share of each accelerator (restarts it)
deployment_detail.action_change: Change its name in the chat, the reply wait or the engine settings
deployment_detail.action_logs: Read its logs and see its errors

deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.description: Every model running on your clusters.
deployments.action_deploy: Deploy a model (the same as Host in the marketplace)
deployments.action_control: Stop, start or delete a deployment
deployments.action_open: Open one for its health, speed and settings

scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.description: Background jobs: model downloads and document ingestion.
scheduler.action_watch: Follow their progress; the list refreshes while jobs run
scheduler.action_retry: Retry a failed job, or cancel a running one

users.title: Users
users.description: The accounts that can sign in. People who only chat need no roles: a new account gets the standard user role.
users.action_create: Create a user with an email address and a first password
users.action_roles: Edit someone's roles and the usage group their usage counts towards
users.action_developer: Developer mode: agents may use local MCP servers on that person's machines
users.action_suspend: Suspend an account, or let it back in
users.action_tokens: See and revoke someone's API tokens

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: A role is a set of permissions. The built-in roles are read-only.
roles.action_create: Create a role and pick its permissions
roles.action_edit: Edit or delete the roles you created

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: A group gives its members roles, and groups their usage in reports.
groups.action_create: Create a group with its roles

auth_providers.title: Sign-in providers
auth_providers.description: Let people sign in with their company account, through OpenID Connect or OAuth2.
auth_providers.action_add: Add a provider with its client ID, secret and discovery URL
auth_providers.action_auto: Choose whether people get an account the first time they sign in

pii_dashboard.title: PII Dashboard
pii_dashboard.description: What the PII filter found in requests, as counts only.
pii_dashboard.action_stats: Scans, detections and the detection rate
pii_dashboard.action_breakdown: Which kinds of personal data, by operation and source

pii_activity.title: PII Activity
pii_activity.description: Every scan and redaction, without the text itself.
pii_activity.action_filter: Filter by operation, by source, or for events with personal data only

pii_policies.title: Tenant PII Policies
pii_policies.description: Override the default PII policy for one tenant. The default policy is under Settings, Modules.
pii_policies.action_load: Pick a tenant and load its policy
pii_policies.action_edit: Choose what is protected for cloud and for local models, and what happens if detection fails
pii_policies.action_preview: See the effective policy before you save

rag_knowledge_base.title: Knowledge Base
rag_knowledge_base.description: Documents the chat can draw on, in nested collections.
rag_knowledge_base.action_upload: Create collections and upload documents; drag to move them
rag_knowledge_base.action_describe: Describe a collection, or let AI write the description
rag_knowledge_base.action_retry: Retry or delete a document that failed

rag_documents.title: Documents
rag_documents.description: Every uploaded document, in one flat list.

rag_collections.title: Collections
rag_collections.description: The collections documents are kept in.

rag_runtime.title: RAG Runtime
rag_runtime.description: The embedding and chunking settings that document search uses.
rag_runtime.action_view: See the embedding model and chunk sizes
rag_runtime.action_edit: Edit them with the full RAG engine; RAG Lite's are under Settings

rag_collectors.title: Collectors
rag_collectors.description: Sources that feed documents in automatically, and their ingestion jobs.

rag_explorer.title: RAG Explorer
rag_explorer.description: Prepare document changes in a draft, then publish them now or at a set time.

rag_publishes.title: Publishes
rag_publishes.description: Publish requests and the ingestion jobs they started. You publish from the Explorer.
rag_publishes.action_watch: Follow publishes; the list refreshes while one runs

rag_search.title: RAG Search
rag_search.description: Try retrieval queries against the indexed documents, with access control applied.
rag_search.action_query: Run a query and see the chunks it finds
rag_search.action_pro: With the full engine: search as a user or group, filter, and choose the mode

chat_projects.title: Chat Projects
chat_projects.description: The projects people created in the chat.
chat_projects.action_delete: Delete a project with all its chats and files

chat_sessions.title: Chat Sessions
chat_sessions.description: Chats by user and project. Titles and messages belong to their users and are not shown here.
chat_sessions.action_browse: See chats by user, status and project

chat_attachments.title: Chat Attachments
chat_attachments.description: Files people attached in the chat, and the storage they use.
chat_attachments.action_browse: See files by user, size and type

mcp_detail.title: MCP Server
mcp_detail.description: One MCP server: its connection and the tools it offers.
mcp_detail.action_tools: Turn single tools on or off
mcp_detail.action_test: Test the connection and count its tools
mcp_detail.action_edit: Edit it; saving reconnects and finds its tools again

mcp_servers.title: MCP Servers
mcp_servers.description: Tool servers that chats and agents can use: search, tickets, files and more.
mcp_servers.action_register: Register a server by URL or command, with its headers or variables
mcp_servers.action_pii: Choose what happens to personal data sent to its tools
mcp_servers.action_scan: Scan the network for MCP servers

skill_detail.title: Skill
skill_detail.description: One skill: its instructions, when it is used, who sees it, and its versions.
skill_detail.action_edit: Edit the instructions and settings, and publish a new version
skill_detail.action_share: Share it, or assign it to a project
skill_detail.action_export: Export it as a SKILL.md or a folder

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Instructions people save once and reuse. In the chat, $ picks one.
skills.action_create: Create a skill, or import a SKILL.md or a zipped skill folder
skills.action_views: See the organization's skills, yours, or the ones shared with you

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Agents that run inside other software (Office, the browser, any application) and are governed by this server. A new agent is a draft: nobody can use it until it is published and granted.
agents.action_create: Create an agent, or start from an app
agents.action_open: Open an agent to change it, publish it and decide who may use it

agent_detail.title: Agent
agent_detail.description: One agent: its definition, its versions, who may use it, and what it did.
agent_detail.action_definition: Change the instructions, model, knowledge and tools; saving makes a new version
agent_detail.action_publish: Publish a version, or roll back to an earlier one
agent_detail.action_access: Grant it to users and teams, and choose its maintainers
agent_detail.action_activity: See its usage, what the applications reported, and the signed-in devices

governance.title: Governance
governance.description: The rules every chat and agent request is held to, and what the checks decided. Changes apply within 30 seconds.
governance.action_rules: Deny, ask first or allow tools by name
governance.action_classes: Say what tools do (read, write, destructive), for the tool modes
governance.action_decisions: Review what the checks decided, without the text

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Settings for the whole system, in three tabs.
settings.action_general: General: every system setting, searchable, and the Hugging Face token
settings.action_modules: Modules: turn optional modules on or off, with their settings

profile.title: My Profile
profile.description: Your account, your password and your API tokens.
profile.action_tokens: Create API tokens for scripts and applications; each is shown once
profile.action_revoke: Revoke a token; applications using it stop within a minute
